explanation: The worked solution confirms F(s)=\int_0^2 e^{(3-s)t}\,dt+2\int_2^\infty e^{-st}\,dt=\frac{e^{2(3-s)}-1}{3-s}+\frac{2e^{-2s}}{s}, converging for s>0. At s=3, the removable singularity is filled by the limit F(3)=2+2e^{-6}/3. The deliberately submitted formula was incorrect; its convergence condition was correct.
